doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: Fraternity life at Alpha Delta
summary: How fraternities were run, house party chaperones, the mix of members and the Alpha Delta house today.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: And you were in a fraternity.
And how were the fraternities different back then.

Well we were a lot freer in our activities, although the college really didn’t like some of the partying that went on. Although at house party time a lot was forgiven. You know I mean the ladies, the dates were housed in the fraternity houses and all the guys had to move out and bunk in the dorms someplace. And so that was an interesting aspect to it. Another interesting aspect was the fact that every house, having a house party with dates in it, had to have a chaperone couple. And the chaperones all met with Sid and Ellie

Wertimer sometime on Friday before the party started, and rules were laid down. And it was pretty much controlled I would say. We had beer available in the house, we had a refrigerator downstairs, so there wasn’t a taboo on that at all. Some of the fraternities were a little wilder than others, depending upon the make-up of the people in it. And in our particular house we had all kinds of people. We had the athletes, we had the scholars, a Rhodes Scholar in one case, musicians, concert guys, you know the choir. We had 65 members at one time, and some of them lived in the dorms but we had to have every bed in the house occupied to keep up with the bills. Anyway, I don’t really know about the fraternity aspect now, I just know that I wish that the fraternity system had not been changed to the extent that it has been. I do get regular reports from my Alpha Delta Phi fraternity here, members and what they’re doing, and really concentrating on literary means, and they’re thinking about if the college will let them do it, with the national fraternity’s assistance, buying a place where they could have meetings off campus. And of course what everyone’s afraid of there in the administration would be that these would be party holes. So I don’t really think it’s ever going to happen but right now the Samuel Eels Memorial Hall was the Alpha Delta House. And it’s been since bought by the college for an unbelievably low amount of money. They expanded it and it’s really a beautiful place, but every time I go in there a lot of the downstairs is still exactly the same: the wallpaper and all that stuff. It really is a very nice place to live and I lived there for 2-1/2 years.
